discriminator.reading: Forest; a small closed form-line loop is drawn about 15-25 m east-north-east of the point, which may mark a rise here before 1899; no structure, pit or building at the point.
Thinned stand, forest floor visible: no structure or debris on the mound.

cited_sources.reading: Isolated round mound at the centre of a forest compartment with fine east-west plough/planting furrows; a disturbed pitted area 60 m north-west; the 500 m view shows rectangular embanked structures and buildings 150-250 m to the north.
Discrete round bright mound centred in the ring.
Coniferous forest with tracks; a small closed form-line loop just east-north-east of the point; another closed loop with a spot height to the north-west.
Walled rectangular structure 60-80 m west; nothing at the centre.

description: A discrete, round, dome-shaped mound about 11 m across and about 1 m high, isolated on flat ground in pine forest.
alt_question: Is this mound connected with the twentieth-century rectangular earthworks and structures nearby (spoil, a blast or cover mound), or a small natural rise of the kind the 1899 form lines suggest, rather than a burial mound?

facts.statement: Rectangular embanked structures and buildings stand 150-250 m north; a walled rectangular structure 60-80 m west.
The 1899 sheet shows forest and a small closed form-line loop near the point.
Only one DGM1 delivery (2016-04-21); no epoch comparison.

limitations: No older DGM1 epoch. Messtischblatt georeferencing unmeasured, so the form-line loop may or may not be this mound. Canopy hides the ground in most DOP frames.
